business_context.summary: This role sits in SimCorp’s Performance & Risk Solutions Engineering pre-sales team and helps win buy-side risk-analytics business before a sale closes. It translates technical risk capabilities into client value, supports sales motions, and feeds prospect feedback back to Product.
business_context.problem_solved: It helps sales teams navigate complex risk use cases and convince sophisticated institutional clients that the risk platform is credible, fit for workflow, and suitable for investment decision-making.
evidence: the job is embedded in the “Performance & Risk Solutions Engineering (‘PreSales’) team,”
its purpose is to support “sales teams navigating complex risk use cases” while also “bringing feedback to the product team”
The role focuses on “multi-asset risk,” “ex-ante risk/tracking error,” “stress testing,” “single security analytics,” and “fixed income products and derivatives”

position_function.function_mix_description: Primarily a technical pre-sales solutions engineering role with a secondary responsibility to relay market feedback to Product and contribute domain risk-analytics expertise.
position_function.reason: The role is explicitly part of the PreSales team, is responsible for discovery, RFPs, demos, and POCs, and must explain the modeling assumptions behind the risk analytics tool. That combination is characteristic of technical solutions engineering rather than delivery or implementation.
evidence: The role is explicitly part of the “PreSales” team.
Responsibilities include “support sales across discovery, request for proposal (RFP), demo, and proof of concept (POC)”
The person must “demo Axioma risk analytics tool and explain the underlying modelling assumptions”
the role also “bring[s] prospect feedback to help improve product”

analyst_notes: This is a technical pre-sales solutions engineering role for buy-side risk analytics. The strongest candidates would combine credible quantitative risk knowledge with client-facing communication, demo skills, and the ability to turn objections and prospect feedback into sales momentum and product input. It is different from implementation roles because the output is deal support and product positioning, not deployment or production support.
